thread:
olivia: quick sync: i've been thinking about the continuous-batching boundary again. current problem: adapters that do aggressive prefetch/warmup end up acting like mini-schedulers and we leak complexity. proposal: explicit "prefetch token" flow plus a lightweight eviction hint to decouple responsibilities. thoughts?

raj: makes sense. can you outline the token lifecycle? curious how revokes and partial-evictions work.

olivia: lifecycle sketch: 1) Adapter asks Scheduler for a PrefetchToken (token_id, soft_ttl_ms, est_credit). 2) Adapter uses token to warm keys; holding token reserves provisional credits. 3) On real dispatch, adapter atomically Redeem(token_id, actual_cost) and scheduler converts provisional -> final. 4) Scheduler can emit EvictHint(token_id, reason) for early cancellation; adapters should stop warmup asap.

maria: clean. add constraint: EvictHint is best-effort and idempotent. scheduler must not assume immediate adapter compliance; it needs to treat missing compliance as stale token and avoid dispatching.

sam: operationally we need TTLs and leak detection. if adapter crashes, tokens must expire quickly and credits return. also metric: orphaned_tokens_count.

raj: race scenarios: adapter redeems token but scheduler concurrently decides to evict (due to higher priority tenant). Redeem must either fail cleanly or win atomically. what's the plan?

olivia: atomicity approach: Redeem performs a two-phase handshake under the scheduler's token shard lock: if token still active -> commit final cost; else Redeem returns Evicted. Retry/fastpath: if Redeem loses, adapter can fallback to non-prefetch path.

maria: two more guardrails: 1) scheduler exposes remaining_ttl_ms in EvictHint so adapter knows whether to abort or hurry, 2) add per-token telemetry: warmup_bytes, warmup_ms, redeem_latency. alert on warmup_ms > 60% of soft_ttl.

sam: for rollout, implement PrefetchToken as opt-in API behind FF. adapters default to current behavior until they opt in. quick experiments at 2% then 20% traffic.

infra-bot: NOTE: created issue #INF-3001 "prefetch-token-eviction-hints" (link: https://redwood/INF-3001)

raj: small optimization: let PrefetchToken carry a backpressure_score instead of raw credits; adapters can pick how aggressively to throttle warmup. keeps scheduler flexible.

olivia: good call. token fields: id, soft_ttl_ms, backpressure_score, warmup_token_ref. keep it tiny. warmup_token_ref points to hotstore with warmup payloads.

maria: add test matrix: concurrent redeem+evict, adapter network partition, scheduler shard failover. and include recovery plan: reconciler that sweeps tokens and reclaims credits.

sam: also add a debug dump endpoint that lists active tokens per adapter for triage (readonly). admin-only.

raj: any perf concerns? token churn rate could explode. recommend batching token grants: adapters can request N tokens in one RPC when they expect bursts.

olivia: yep will add bulk AcquireTokens API. also compact token ids (base62) to reduce memory and wire overhead.

maria: ok next steps: olivia to draft small RFC addendum + sequence diagrams; raj to prototype redeem/evict atomicity logic; sam to write failure test harness. we'll track in INF-3001.

olivia: will post draft later today. thanks all :sparkles:
